consumer_seed: The Ofcom adult media and online lives news release was published on 2 April 2026.
The release summarises findings from Ofcom's Adults’ Media Use and Attitudes and Adults’ Media Lives research.
Ofcom reported that 89% of adult internet users used at least one social media platform.
Ofcom reported that social-media use rose to 97% among 16–34-year-olds.
Ofcom reported that 49% of adult social-media users actively posted, shared or commented, down from 61% in 2024.
Ofcom reported that the proportion exploring new websites fell from 70% to 56%.
Ofcom reported that concern about online posts causing future problems rose to 49% from 43%.
Ofcom reported that 59% of online adults felt the benefits of being online outweighed the risks, down from 72%.
Ofcom reported that 36% of social-media users said platforms were good for their mental health, down from 42%.
Ofcom reported that 67% said they sometimes spent too long on devices and 40% said this happened most days.
Ofcom reported that 54% of UK adults used AI tools.
Ofcom reported AI-tool use of 79% among 16–24-year-olds and 74% among 25–34-year-olds.
Ofcom reported that 12% of AI users used the tools conversationally, rising to 19% among 25–34-year-olds.
Ofcom reported overall online confidence of 89%, compared with 81% for recognising advertising and 72% for judging accuracy.
Ofcom reported that 82% indicated a safe response to a scam email, down from 88% in 2022.
The Ofcom online-communities research page was published on 24 June 2026.
The research used a multi-stage mixed-methods design with adults and children aged 13–17 who use online communities.
The research defines persuasive design as service-design features that can influence user behaviour.
Ofcom reported that 79% of UK adults said they had ever used an online community.
Ofcom reported that 78% of 13–17-year-olds said they had ever used an online community.
